text:
alex: Heads up — us-west-2 dedicated saw a ~3-4x tail latency spike on text-gen between 08:10-08:25 UTC. Throughput also dropped ~30%.
priya: saw it on the dashboards, was just about to ping. Any recent deploys to the kernel selector or admission code? :thinking_face:
marcos: rolled kernel-selector v2.3.1 at 07:50 UTC (small change: prefer fused kernels for 1.5B-6B ranges). Admission controller was unchanged.
jin: looking at profiler dumps now. microbatch sizes collapsed — median microbatch went from 10 -> 2 for many workers. That matches throughput drop.
lia: I'm seeing a surge of KV-cache evictions on a subset of shards during the same window. eviction rate spiked ~6x. Possibly fragmentation causing smaller effective prefixes?
alex: hmm — maybe fused kernels increased single-token latency and admission started shaving batches to hit latency SLOs. Any evidence kernel latency per step increased?
jin: captured traces: new fused kernel path adds ~0.8ms per token on 8K seq workloads vs previous kernel for certain attention shapes. Not huge but with microbatching it compounds.
marcos: the selector change includes a heuristic: if predicted token cost > threshold, pick fused kernels; threshold tuned yesterday. Could be misprediction for some models.
priya: so the flow might be: kernel choice -> per-step slowness -> admission sees longer in-flight -> reduces allowed microbatch -> more small microbatches -> KV cache miss amplification + evictions -> tail spikes. Does that map?
lia: yes that maps to the metrics. Also small microbatches increase KV cache churn because prefix keys are less likely to be reused across incoming requests.
sre-bot: incident-note: created incident INC-2026-042, assigned eng-runtime oncall.
alex: immediate mitigation proposals:
- revert kernel-selector to v2.3.0 on us-west-2 (canary) OR
- increase admission latency window to be less reactive (buffer a bit) OR
- temporarily pin batching min size to 8 for dedicated pool
Which should we try first?
marcos: quick revert is easiest and fastest to validate whether kernel selector is root cause. I'll prepare a canary revert patch.
jin: while waiting, I'll run pprof on a few hot inference containers and dump kernel timing histograms to S3. `kubectl exec -c infer -- pprof /metrics > /tmp/pprof && gzip /tmp/pprof`
lia: I'll snapshot KV cache metrics and export the hot-key list to see if eviction targets align with tenant IDs.
priya: agree with revert first. If MARCOS can't push fast enough, we can pin min microbatch size as a hotfix to stop fragmentation.
marcos: starting canary revert rollout now to a single AZ (us-west-2a). switching selector image to r2.3.0-canary.
alex: monitoring logs. alert if p50 gen > 50ms or tail > 500ms.
jin: pprof uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1987654322/pprof.tar.gz — histograms show 0.9ms extra on fused path for attn-loop at 512 tokens.
lia: KV snapshot: hot-shard owners: tenant-77, tenant-13, tenant-3. Eviction policy looks normal, but eviction bursts coincide with admission drops.
priya: after canary revert, p50/p95 improved in that AZ within two minutes. Other AZs still degraded.
marcos: rolling revert to all AZs now.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: rolling update started for kernel-selector -> r2.3.0-canary (4/4 pods updated)
alex: good. keep monitoring for 15m window.
jin: post-revert histograms show fused kernel path usage dropped from 82% -> 12% on these workloads.
lia: KV eviction rate back to normal. microbatch median back to 9-11.
priya: root cause: selector heuristic threshold misclassified common attention shapes as 'fused-faster' when in practice it regressed for our token distribution, leading to cascading admission and KV churn.
marcos: open PR to add a safety-net: require A/B microbenchmarks (short-run sampling) before switching kernel on production traffic, and add a decay factor to avoid oscillation.
alex: also log per-request kernel decision and predicted vs observed latency so we can detect bad mappings faster.
priya: action items:
- marcos: PR for canary gating + revert (in progress) — due today
- jin: attach perf histograms to the incident and add automated alert if selector causes >5% microbatch shrink for 5m
- lia: add KV eviction spike alert tied to microbatch median drop
- alex: follow up with postmortem template

marcos: FYI I'll also bump the admission controller's hysteresis to avoid reacting to single-minute blips while we tune selector.
alex: thanks team. great fast response. closing thread when incident is resolved.
